- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20% for short-term spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 5–15% buffer to low-end forecasts for 30-day horizon.
- Model consistently overpredicts high-value days (e.g., 7–10+ in forecast) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; cap such forecasts at 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early 30-day window; adjust for 10–15% downward bias in first 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00) are common; apply 2–3 day decay factor to forecasted peaks to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast smoothing.
